props.title: Small Wonders

sections.content: **Small Wonders (1996)** (1996) stands among the most powerful documentaries about music education ever made. Following violin teacher Roberta Guaspari's fight to keep music programs alive in East Harlem public schools, it inspired the feature film **Music of the Heart** (1999) starring Meryl Streep. The documentary captures raw, transformative moments as inner-city students discover classical music, echoing similar themes found in **Mr. Holland's Opus** (1995) and **School of Rock** (2003), but with the gritty authenticity only real-life footage can deliver. sections.content: The film arrived during a crucial period of education documentaries in the 1990s, alongside **High School II** (1994) and **Children in America's Schools** (1996), exposing both the challenges and possibilities within American public education. Director Allan Miller, known for his classical music documentaries like **From Mao to Mozart: Isaac Stern in China** (1979), brings an expert eye to capturing both the technical aspects of music instruction and the emotional journey of the students. SUBHEAD: Impact on Education Documentary Genre

**Small Wonders** (1996) helped establish the template for future education documentaries like **Mad Hot Ballroom** (2005) and **Brooklyn Castle** (2012), focusing on how arts and enrichment programs transform disadvantaged students. The film's vérité style, avoiding narrator intervention, lets the pure drama of classroom breakthroughs and administrative battles tell the story, influencing later works like **Waiting for Superman** (2010).
